files_measured: $WORK/engines/subreg/src/subreg.c (706 lines, the only engine TU; subreg.h is header-only; tests/subreg-tests.c + tests/cutest.h excluded as test code)
excluded_functions: none - all 12 functions in the per-function breakdown are engine code (sum 1704 = file total). parse_repetition/parse_concatenation/parse_sub_expr/parse_expr are inlined by gcc.
per_function_top: parse_literal 788; decode_non_class_metacharacter 292; parse_alternation 178; subreg_match 128; skip_block 104; decode_hex 66; match_char.isra.0 38; match_word 32 (then match_hexadecimal 28, match_whitespace 20, invert_match 18, match_digit 12)
libc_deps: NONE. arm-none-eabi-nm -u on the Cortex-M4 object prints nothing: no malloc, no strlen, no memcmp, no setjmp, no ctype; subreg.c includes only subreg.h.
ram_model: No malloc, no static/global data (data=0 bss=0). State is one ~32-byte state_t on the stack plus a caller-supplied capture array (8 B per capture on 32-bit: pointer+unsigned). Recursion only through nested groups: cycle parse_literal(40 B frame) -> parse_alternation(24 B) per nesting level (~64 B/level, gcc -fstack-usage, Cortex-M4) + 48 B for subreg_match; depth is capped by the caller's max_depth argument (error -6 beyond it). Repetition is a loop, not recursion, so input length does not grow the stack. No pattern compilation step: the regex string is re-parsed while matching (interpreter over the pattern text).
features_verified: READ FROM SOURCE (subreg.c): literals; '.' = any byte except NUL (DOES match \n); escapes \f \n \r \t \v \xXX and \b = BACKSPACE (not word boundary); \d\D \w\W \s\S plus non-standard \h\H (hex digit) and \!X (negated single char); unknown \X = literal X; quantifiers ? * + only, greedy AND POSSESSIVE (parse_repetition loops the item until it fails, never gives back); NO {n,m} (braces are literal chars); NO lazy quantifiers ('a*?' = 'a*' followed by literal '?'); alternation '|' ordered/first-match but ATOMIC (never re-entered after a later failure), and an empty first alternative ('|x', '(|a)') is mis-parsed as a literal '|'; groups: () capturing, (?:) non-capturing, (?=) (?!) lookahead; inline (?i)/(?I) ASCII-only case folding scoped to the enclosing group (no API flag - driver prefixes '(?i)'); classes [..] [^..] with ranges, but a-b is a range only if the char after '-' is [0-9A-Za-z_], backslash inside [] is a literal (no [\d], no [\]]), ']' first is literal; anchors: match is ALWAYS anchored at both ends (whole-input match), leading '^' and trailing '$' are just skipped, '^'/'$' elsewhere = literal / syntax error; no search/find API (driver scans start positions); captures: index assigned in COMPLETION order (inner groups before outer), one new entry per repetition of a quantified group (so (a)* on long input overflows -> error -7), entries from a failed alternative are not removed, unmatched optional groups get no entry (no -1/-1 concept); byte-wise only, no UTF-8 awareness; no backreferences, no \b word boundary, no multiline, no POSIX classes. README claim 'non-backtracking, greedy and possessive' is accurate.
difftest: corpus_seed1: cases=2088 checked=2081 pass=1489 fail=592 timeouts=15 group_spans_checked=47 (driver wraps pattern as '(?i)?(?:PAT)(.*)' and scans start positions; end = start of the trailing (.*) capture). Failure classification (classify.py, each failure assigned one bucket): MISSING FEATURE 435 = 271 {n,m} counted repetition + 117 lazy quantifiers *? +? ?? + 47 escapes/\d\w\s inside [ ]; SEMANTICS 133 = 119 byte-wise matching of UTF-8 ('.', [^x], quantifiers consume one byte) + 7 error -7 capture overflow (one capture per repetition, e.g. (a*)*) + 5 capture numbering/lifetime (completion order, per-iteration entries, stale entry from failed alternative, e.g. (a)|(b) on 'b' reports group1=[0,1]) + 2 '.' matches newline; BUG 24 = 15 hang/TIMEOUT (infinite loop in parse_repetition when the repeated item matches empty, e.g. (?:a*)*, (?:)*, (?:a?)+ - reproduced through the raw API in hang.c, no driver involved) + 9 empty first alternative parsed as literal '|' ('|x' on 'xc' -> nomatch, expected [0,0]). Possessive/atomic no-backtracking semantics caused 0 of the failures: a Python 3.11 possessive/atomic oracle shows that none of the 195 ASCII, subreg-parsable corpus cases needs backtracking, so the 1489 pass count OVERSTATES compatibility; hand tests: a*a/'aaa' -> nomatch, (a|ab)c/'abc' -> nomatch (Perl: match).
caveats: (1) subreg has no search API and no end-of-match report, so the driver adapts: pattern wrapped as '(?:PAT)(.*)' (a trailing unescaped '$' drops the (.*), a leading '^' restricts to start 0), start positions scanned leftmost-first; max_captures=64, max_depth=64; any negative return is printed as 'error N'. This exposes the engine's own possessive semantics faithfully (no extra backtracking added). (2) Group spans are printed in subreg's completion order so nested-group numbering differs from Perl by design. (3) measure.sh reports Cortex-M0+ (1556) SMALLER than Cortex-M4 (1704) - reported as measured, not investigated. (4) The 1704 B includes features outside the target spec (lookahead, (?i)/(?I) inline options, \h, \!, \xXX) and lacks {n,m}, lazy, UTF-8, class escapes, search - so it is not a like-for-like size reference for the proposed engine. (5) Pattern is interpreted directly from the string on every match (no compile step) - this is where the small size comes from, and also the source of the empty-match hang (no progress check at subreg.c:558-571). (6) With -w warnings are suppressed; the code has a non-standard 'typedef enum {...} mode_t' that shadows POSIX mode_t if <sys/types.h> is included (compiled fine here because subreg.c includes only subreg.h). (7) Nothing was modified in the engine source.
